references.text: The place Jesus found in the scroll was exactly this prophecy from Isaiah, which he read aloud in the synagogue (quoted in Luke 4:18-19).
Ezra opened the Book of the Law and read from it to the people, a parallel to Jesus' reading from Scripture in the synagogue.
In Antioch of Pisidia, readings were also taken from the Law and the Prophets in the synagogue, reflecting the Jewish custom of scripture reading that Jesus also participated in.
Moses is read aloud in the synagogues every Sabbath, confirming the established practice of scripture reading that we see Jesus taking part in here.
The following verses reproduce the content of the passage from Isaiah that Jesus found and read aloud from the scroll.
A reference to the Book of the Lord (scroll), pointing to the tradition of preserving and reading prophetic writings.
Jesus rolled up the scroll again after the reading, completing the action of opening it in verse 17.
